{{Short description|Algebraic structure in semigroup theory}}
In [[mathematics]], a '''nowhere commutative semigroup''' is a [[semigroup]] ''S'' such that, for all ''a'' and ''b'' in ''S'', if ''ab'' = ''ba'' then ''a'' = ''b''.<ref name=CP>[[A. H. Clifford]], [[G. B. Preston]] (1964). ''The Algebraic Theory of Semigroups Vol. I'' (Second Edition). [[American Mathematical Society]] (p.26). {{ISBN|978-0-8218-0272-4}}</ref> A semigroup ''S'' is nowhere commutative [[if and only if]] any two elements of ''S'' are [[inverse semigroup|inverses]] of each other.<ref name="CP"/>

==Characterization of nowhere commutative semigroups==

Nowhere commutative semigroups can be [[characterization (mathematics)|characterized]] in several different ways. If ''S'' is a semigroup then the following statements are [[logical equivalence|equivalent]]:<ref name=Howie>{{cite book|last=J. M. Howie|title=An Introduction to Semigroup Theory|publisher=Academic Press|year=1976|series=LMS monographs|volume= 7|pages=96}}</ref>
*''S'' is nowhere commutative.
*''S'' is a [[rectangular band]] (in the sense in which the term is used by [[John Mackintosh Howie|John Howie]]<ref>
{{cite book|last=J. M. Howie|title=An Introduction to Semigroup Theory|publisher=Academic Press|year=1976|series=LMS monographs|volume= 7|pages=3}}</ref>).
*For all ''a'' and ''b'' in ''S'',  ''aba'' = ''a''.
*For all ''a'', ''b'' and ''c'' in ''S'', ''a''<sup>2</sup> = ''a'' and ''abc'' = ''ac''.

Even though, by definition, the rectangular bands are concrete semigroups, they have the defect that their definition is formulated not in terms of the basic [[binary operation]] in the semigroup. The approach via the definition of  nowhere commutative semigroups rectifies this defect.<ref name=Howie/>

To see that a nowhere commutative semigroup is a rectangular band, let ''S'' be a nowhere commutative semigroup. Using the defining properties of a nowhere commutative semigroup, one can see that for every ''a'' in ''S'' the [[Intersection (mathematics)|intersection]] of the [[Green's relations|Green classes]] ''R''<sub>''a''</sub> and ''L''<sub>''a''</sub> contains the unique element ''a''. Let ''S''{{space|hair}}/{{space|hair}}''L'' be the family of ''L''-classes in ''S'' and ''S''{{space|hair}}/{{space|hair}}''R'' be the family of ''R''-classes in ''S''. The mapping
:ψ : ''S '' → (''S''{{space|hair}}/{{space|hair}}''R'') × (''S''{{space|hair}}/{{space|hair}}''L'')
defined by 
:''a''ψ = (''R''<sub>''a''</sub>{{space|hair}}, ''L''<sub>''a''</sub>)
is a [[bijection]]. If the [[Cartesian product]] (''S''{{space|hair}}/{{space|hair}}''R'') × (''S''{{space|hair}}/{{space|hair}}''L'') is made into a semigroup  by furnishing it with the rectangular band multiplication, the map ψ becomes an [[isomorphism]]. So ''S'' is isomorphic to a rectangular band.

Other claims of equivalences follow directly from the relevant definitions.
